description: Evaluation cases for the internet-identity-sso skill. Tests whether agents configure an organization's discovery file correctly: whole-file rejection on one bad value, exact-origin app_clients keys, and the stable identifier claim per provider.

output_evals.name: Adversarial: one bad value rejects the whole discovery file
output_evals.prompt: We want sessions through our Internet Identity SSO domain to last as long as the provider allows, so I set session_max_age_seconds to 0 in our /.well-known/ii-openid-configuration meaning no limit. Our users can no longer sign in with the company domain at all. Is that related?
expected_behaviors: States that 0 is rejected, not treated as unlimited, and that the valid range is above 0 up to 2592000 seconds (30 days)
Explains that Internet Identity rejects the ENTIRE file on one bad value, so SSO becomes unavailable for the whole domain rather than falling back to the default
Says the value is rejected rather than clamped
Mentions that getSsoStatus() reads unavailable for the domain while the file is invalid
Does NOT suggest the provider or the OIDC client is misconfigured as the first explanation

output_evals.name: Adversarial: app_clients key must be the app's exact origin
output_evals.prompt: I added "https://payroll.acme.com/": "0oaPAYROLL" to app_clients in our ii-openid-configuration so payroll gets its own OIDC client with its own group assignment. Staff who are not in the payroll group can still sign in to it. What did I get wrong?
expected_behaviors: Identifies the trailing slash as the problem: the key must be the app's exact origin, with no trailing slash, no path and the same scheme
Explains that a key that does not match is not an error: the app silently falls back to the organization's default client_id, which is why the group assignment has no effect
Shows the corrected entry keyed by https://payroll.acme.com
Mentions gate_all_apps as the way to refuse apps that are not listed, if that is the intent
Does NOT claim the provider ignores group assignment or that per-app clients are unsupported

output_evals.name: Adversarial: stable identifier claim on Entra ID
output_evals.prompt: We're configuring Internet Identity SSO against Microsoft Entra ID and giving two of our apps their own OIDC clients. Should I set stable_identifier_claim, or is the default fine?
expected_behaviors: Says stable_identifier_claim must be set to "oid" for Entra ID, because its sub differs per client
Explains the consequence of leaving the default sub with per-app clients: the same person keys onto a different identity in each app
Notes that changing stable_identifier_claim on a live domain is a migration, not a config tweak, because it changes how identities key onto anchors
Does NOT recommend email or preferred_username as the stable identifier

trigger_evals.description: Queries to test whether the skill activates correctly.
should_trigger: Set up Internet Identity sign-in for our staff against our Okta tenant
Publish the ii-openid-configuration file for our company domain
Give one of our apps its own OIDC client in the Internet Identity SSO config
Our Internet Identity SSO domain reads unavailable and we published the file
We changed our discovery file and Internet Identity is still using the old one
should_not_trigger: Let my app send users to their company's SSO
Add Internet Identity login to my frontend
Sign in with a Google account on Internet Identity
Read the user's verified email in my canister
